skill.name: worldview-synthesis
skill.description: Guides users through structured questions to articulate beliefs, values, tensions, and worldview narratives for personal, leadership, or organizational reflection.
skill.summary: Map beliefs into clear principles, tensions, and narrative worldview documents.
skill.author: 2389-research

content.value_statement: Many people have beliefs but struggle to explain how they connect. This skill turns answers into a structured worldview and polished narrative.
actual_capabilities: Creates a worldview project structure with data and narrative sections.
Collects shaping sources and extracts three to five key ideas from each one.
Runs guided interrogation rounds across ethics, work, trust, money, and future orientation.
Identifies tensions between beliefs and records them as embraced, resolved, or unresolved.
Generates mission, thesis, synopsis, and long-form narrative outputs at increasing depth.
Provides ready-made question sets and a YAML-style belief schema for organization.
limitations: It does not verify whether personal beliefs are factually correct.
It may surface sensitive topics that require user consent and care.
It depends on honest user answers and source descriptions.
It is not a substitute for therapy, legal advice, or spiritual counseling.

use_cases.title: Personal Values Clarification
use_cases.description: An individual can explore core beliefs and convert them into a mission statement and principles.

use_cases.title: Leadership Philosophy Drafting
use_cases.description: A founder or manager can document decision principles, tensions, and culture beliefs before sharing them with a team.

use_cases.title: Manifesto Development
use_cases.description: A writer can organize sources, claims, and contradictions before drafting a public worldview essay.

prompt_templates.title: Start My Worldview Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use the worldview-synthesis skill. Ask me the first round of questions and record my initial belief nodes.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Belief Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask me about books, people, experiences, and articles that shaped me. Extract three to five key ideas from each source.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Tensions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my belief notes. Identify tensions, name each one clearly, and suggest whether it is embraced, resolved, or unresolved.

prompt_templates.title: Create Full Narrative
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my ideas, sources, and tensions to draft a mission, thesis, synopsis, and full worldview narrative in my voice.

output_examples.input: I know my views on work, family, and politics, but they feel scattered.
output_examples.output: A structured belief map with domains, source influences, confidence levels, and named tensions for later writing.

output_examples.input: I need a leadership philosophy for my new team.
output_examples.output: A concise mission statement, five to seven principles, and a one-page thesis for team discussion.

output_examples.input: I selected answers that conflict with each other.
output_examples.output: A tension summary that names the conflict and marks it as embraced, resolved, or unresolved.

best_practices: Start with real sources and experiences before abstract principles.
Keep low-confidence beliefs visible instead of forcing certainty.
Review generated narratives with the user before sharing them externally.
anti_patterns: Do not treat questionnaire options as a complete worldview.
Do not smooth away contradictions that matter to the user.
Do not publish personal narratives without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill write a manifesto?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn structured beliefs into mission, thesis, synopsis, and longer narrative formats.

faq.question: Does it make decisions for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize beliefs and tensions so you can make your own decisions.

faq.question: Can it handle sensitive topics?
faq.answer: Yes, but use care. It asks about mortality, ethics, relationships, money, conflict, and future concerns.

faq.question: Does it require source material?
faq.answer: No. Sources improve the result, but the skill can start from answers and experiences.

faq.question: Can teams use it?
faq.answer: Yes. Leaders can adapt it to document leadership philosophy or company culture principles.

faq.question: Will it resolve contradictions?
faq.answer: Not always. It names tensions and can mark them as embraced, resolved, or unresolved.
